title: P-MIDNIGHT (log-only probe, user-preapproved class, 2026-09-27): host + client on save1 cross midnight - the host's day roll is marked ('[Midnight] day roll begin/end'), the client's market apply logs begin (bytes) / end (ms, rows, steps); a DEV main-thread block on the client ('stalltest 8') is named by the stall watchdog with its step, the live ring log is flushed to disk, and the resume is logged
preconditions: Fixture save1 (host melaus, client Client1). Dev build with the P-MIDNIGHT probe (src/StallWatch.cs) and the 'stalltest' lever. No save is taken.
oracles_absent: \[Stall\] (watchdog:|watchdog start:|ring flush:|rotate:|day-roll step target|ring log fields)

steps.note: the client is served its save and settles
the watchdog runs on the client

expect_log.regex: \[Midnight\] market apply end \d+ ms \(\d+ rows, \d+ steps\)

steps.note: TEST P-MIDNIGHT (b): the host's own clock path to 3 game-minutes before midnight; live time crosses it (NewDay marked step by step); the client's next market snapshot apply logs begin + end with rows and the step count

steps.expect_result: ^OK stalltest blocked the main thread 8 s

expect_log.regex: \[Stall\] main thread stuck \d+\.\d s at step 'dev stalltest' \(#8 'stalltest'\)

steps.note: TEST P-MIDNIGHT (c): the main thread blocked 8 s (DEV) - the watchdog names the step once, flushes the ring log, then logs the resume

steps.expect_result: ^OK stallwatch thread=alive stalls=[1-9]\d* resumed=[1-9]\d* stallflush=[1-9]\d* ringwrites=[1-9]\d* ringbytes=[1-9]\d* ringage=1?\d\.\ds
steps.note: TEST P-MIDNIGHT (a): the live ring file (bamp-ring-live-<install>.log) is on disk and was written in the last 20 s
